npcs.name: Guardian Tofor Brotoras
npcs.description: Stern, honorable, and quick to anger, Tofor is proud to serve on the council. After losing many friends (and one of her own arms) in the struggles against the Chroma Conclave, she took the vulnerability of the city to heart, swearing never to allow such a thing to happen again. She is a beloved hero of the war against the Chroma Conclave and has served on the council since before the death of the Last Sovereign. Most folk in Emon suspect she'll win reelection until the day she dies.

npcs.name: Seeker Odessa Tal'Dorei
npcs.description: When the eldest daughter of the Last Sovereign campaigned for the Master of Information's seat, its current holder was Seeker Assum Emring, a loyal servant of her father's. He bowed out of the race, and his blithe quote made headlines in Emon: "I taught her everything she knows." She won in a landslide. Odessa wields the dual blades of Assum's spy network and the mercenary agents of the Clasp with practiced finesse. Nevertheless, her name and the legacy of her father's martyrdom weigh heavily upon her. As Seeker, Odessa is calm, methodical, and laconic, but she carries a dignified sorrow.

npcs.name: Arcanist Allura Vysoren
npcs.description: Allura Vysoren has held the position of Master of Arcana since before the Chroma Conclave's attack, and is held in the esteem of Tal'Dorei's people—mages and common folk alike. As a member of the Arcana Pansophical, she is also increasingly worried as politicians fall in debt to the League of Miracles. After decades of investigating supernatural abnormalities herself, age has finally forced her to limit her adventuresome excursions. She now is one of the council's foremost employers of adventurers.

npcs.name: Arbiter Brom Goldhand
npcs.description: As stone-faced, gray-haired, flame-scarred cleric of the Knowing Mentor, Brom is as mysterious as he is proficient with law. One thing is clear: he is dedicated to keeping the realm just and orderly, and there are few who would dare challenge his judgement.

npcs.name: Hearthmaker Edelbern Cleareyes
npcs.description: As a goliath of the Rivermaw nomads, no one expected Edelbern to have an interest in civic architecture. Yet, after growing up in Westruun while it was occupied by the Herd of Storms some twenty years ago, he found that he preferred the beauty of stone towers to towering pines. He also possessed a remarkable gift of mathematical acuity, and used his skills to set Westruun—and eventually all of Tal'Dorei—on the path of reconstruction. Edelbern is also idealistic to a fault, and has, in his dedication to restoration, been manipulated into handing numerous lucrative contracts to the League of Miracles, allowing them to amass greater and greater power.

npcs.name: Coinmistress Vex'ahlia de Rolo
npcs.description: As a member of Vox Machina and hero of the realm, Vex'ahlia could help Tal'Dorei in any number of ways. She already held a ceremonial title in Whitestone as Grand Mistress of the Grey Hunt. Yet when she and her husband pushed for Whitestone to be formally recognized as a constituent city of the Republic of Tal'Dorei, all who knew her name (and her legendary financial savvy) clamored for her to be elected to the council as Coinmistress. She took to the duty with aplomb, and fights hard to ensure that Emon never gets the bad end of a deal when gold is involved.

npcs.name: Ambassador Syldor Vessar
npcs.description: Vex'ahlia's elven father has served as his city's ambassador to Emon for well over a century, and requested to be appointed a seated ambassador as soon as the office was created. Though he is otherwise a staunch traditionalist, Syldor was inspired by his brave children to move past his old racial prejudices and drive his homeland to be less bigoted and xenophobic—learning from his own mistakes as a father to two half-elven children. His relationship with his elder daughter is still strained, and it is a newsworthy occasion when they vote in accord.

npcs.name: Ambassador Deirdrik Greyspine
npcs.description: The youngest son of the ruling House Greyspine of Kraghammer, Deirdrik has little hope of being elected Ironkeeper. Instead, this ambitious young dwarf—a scant seventy years old—left his home to win political renown in the national arena. He is a romantic idealist at heart and always votes for bold new policies, but doesn't always think through the consequences of his actions.

npcs.name: Ambassador Keyleth of the Ashari
npcs.description: A legendary archdruid and member of Vox Machina, Keyleth is both leader of the Air Ashari and ambassador for all Tal'Dorei's Ashari peoples. She despises politics, and is focused entirely on improving the wellbeing of as many people as possible—as well as involving the Ashari on the national stage. She spends most of her time in Zephrah, with her people—including her father, Korrin, and her newly returned mother, Vilya—but she can and will arrive in Emon at the drop of a hat, if Vex asks it of her.

npcs.name: Delegate Kel'jaia Uloeh
npcs.description: Kel'jaia is a confident gnome with incredible strength and resilience—both physical and emotional. She is thought by all to be the council's first choice for Master of War, should the time ever call for it. She was born in the Rifenmist Jungle and grew up amidst mercenaries who fought against the Iron Authority. After her commander was killed in battle, she traveled north to Syngorn to seek aid in her fight. She dreams of forging bonds of unity between her homeland and Tal'Dorei.

npcs.name: Magus Seanor Wiles
npcs.description: A humble-looking traveler, Wiles delights in finding fresh and emerging talent and helping his new students refine their arcane gifts.

npcs.name: Planerider Ryn
npcs.description: This former pupil of Yurek Windseeker has grown into a master of planar travel. She likewise has taken an interest in the flow of magic across the world by means of ley lines. She's constantly on the move, traveling from plane to plane to conduct her research.

npcs.name: Tinkerer Quash Dentdruggle
npcs.description: Obsessed with the development of autonomous and living arcane constructs, Quash is usually holed up in his laboratory within Kraghammer.

npcs.name: Elementalist Drake Thunderbrand
npcs.description: Driven to bind the physical elements of the chaotic planes to his will, Drake is a prodigy of new incantations in the field. He and Allura Vysoren are lifelong friends, and together they're renowned for achieving the impossible.

npcs.name: Realmseer Eskil Ryndarien
npcs.description: Though he was a Maker for most of his life, Realmseer Ryndarien grew frustrated with the politics and factions of the Pansophical, eventually retiring to Westruun to pursue his own interests. These days, he has found a way to rejuvenate his aged body and is now renowned as a handsome and aloof man about town—much to the annoyance of all who formerly knew him.

npcs.name: Pa'tice, Heart of the Mountain
npcs.description: Elderly leader of the Earth Ashari, Pa'tice still shows vigor and strength to resist his age, having led his people through many very tough challenges. His stubbornness is legendary, and it's said even death has been forced to wait until Pa'tice sees it his proper time. Many believe that his druidic training will keep him alive until he himself chooses to let go of this mortal coil.

npcs.name: Korrin of Zephrah
npcs.description: His wife Vilya was lost while she undertook the Aramente, and when the previous Voice of the Tempest died of illness, Korrin was called upon to act as Voice until his daughter Keyleth came of age and completed her Aramente. Korrin was shocked when, Vilya suddenly returned, and now spends his days in disbelieving bliss, reunited with his long-lost wife. He is gentle with those who show honor, and merciless to those who threaten his people.

npcs.name: Vilya, Who Escaped Death
npcs.description: Vilya disappeared on her Aramente nearly thirty years ago, and was presumed dead. Her daughter, Keyleth, took up her own Aramente ten years after Vilya left, and discovered from the Water Ashari of Vesrah that Vilya was killed by a kraken, and only her leg was able to be recovered. Less than a year ago, Vilya suddenly strode out of a tree in Zephrah, her leg replaced with a druidic prosthetic of her own creation, shocking all—though none were more overwhelmed with emotion than her daughter and husband. Though Vilya never earned the title of Voice of the Tempest, she now aids her daughter in leading her people without the faintest trace of jealousy.

npcs.name: Keyleth, Voice of the Tempest
npcs.description: Hero of Tal'Dorei and member of Vox Machina, Keyleth completed her Aramente and took leadership among her people following the destruction of the Chroma Conclave. She seems to have not aged a day since Vox Machina's victory over the Whispered One. Since her beloved's death, she has kept busy to fill the void in her heart. From expanding the crisis orb network across the realm and building beautiful windmills in the Summit Peaks with Percy's aid to

npcs.name: Lady Cassandra Johanna de Rolo
npcs.description: Cassandra is Percival's younger sister, thought dead until he discovered her in the thrall of the Briarwoods. She now manages Whitestone's most pressing matters, with daily briefings from other members of the chamber, She is beloved throughout the city for her resilience and her decisive leadership.

npcs.name: Cassandra de Rolo
npcs.description: Human head of the Chamber of Whitestone. Cassandra is Percival's younger sister, thought dead until he discovered her in the thrall of the Briarwoods. She now manages Whitestone’s most pressing matters, with daily briefings from other members of the chamber, She is beloved throughout the city for her resilience and her decisive leadership.

npcs.name: Lord Percival Fredrickstein von Musel Klossowski de Rolo III
npcs.description: Human member of the Chamber of Whitestone. Percival is Cassandra's older brother, thought dead Vox Machina discovered him in a prison cell. His life was filled with countless joys and regrets. He has taken well to retirement from adventuring, and is renowned across Tal'Dorei for his creations.

npcs.name: Lady Vex'ahlia de Rolo
npcs.description: Half-Elf Member of the Chamber of Whitestone. Vex'ahlia is the Grand Mistress of the Grey Hunt, a title she has held since before she married Percival. Over the past twenty-four years, she has become a talented and respected leader of the Grey Hunters. And though the hunters use guns inspired by her husband’s own designs, she still prefers to wield her trusty bow.

npcs.name: Grog Strongjaw
npcs.description: Goliath friend. The noble, if simple, warrior of Vox Machina, no one really knows if Grog’s title is a real title at all, or if Percy was just joking when he gave it to him. Grog likes it, and that's good enough for most people.

npcs.name: Claret Director Alasterre de Vitrevos
npcs.description: Calm and sanguine to a fault, Alasterre de Vitrevos is the youngest-ever director of Tal'Dorei's Claret Order. He sees his position as one he deserves without question, and is willing to use his command more boldly than his mentor, director emeritus Teresa Dulamar. He is frequently seen in the field, working with various adventuring parties and his own blood hunters to wipe out monsters wherever they emerge. The combination of his relaxed personality and his aggressive strategy may seem a contradiction at first glance, but those who know him see the truth of the immense self-assurance that lets him make hard decisions without hesitation. This quality is a strength when coolheaded leadership is needed in the thick of battle, but it can make him challenging to work with as an equal.

npcs.name: Director Emeritus Teresa Dulamar
npcs.description: The former head of Tal'Dorei's Claret Orders retired ten years ago after suffering a traumatic death in combat. Her soul accepted resurrection, but she took her defeat as a sign to let younger, fresher blood take her place. She remains a part of the Claret Orders to advise the current director on matters he is too young to have experienced himself. Though she displays a chilly demeanor, she simply keeps her compassionate side hidden from the untrusted riffraff.

npcs.name: Hunter Jorick Lamensh
npcs.description: Once among the greatest of all blood hunters, Jorick is now Director Emeritus Teresa Dulamar's personal bodyguard. He is still a capable member of the Order of the Profane Soul, and urges immediate, decisive action to destroy demons and devils whenever their occult activity is discovered.

npcs.name: Spireling Shenn
npcs.description: A powerful illusionist, Shenn runs a far-reaching network of spies and informants. In his younger days, he was a canny negotiator who sought to spread the Clasp beyond Tal'Dorei. The arrival of the Myriad forced the Clasp onto the defensive, and he will never forgive them for souring his ambitions.

npcs.name: Spireling Warren
npcs.description: Deadly duelist turned master assassin of the Clasp, Warren handles all contracts that involve kidnapping, assassination, and intimidation. He hates public appearances.

npcs.name: Spireling Zilloa
npcs.description: An accomplished burglar, Zilloa has risen to the head of all thieving, smuggling, and black-market dealings within the Clasp of Emon. She plays a dangerous game by enjoying folk hero status as the public liaison between the Clasp and the Tal'Dorei Council.

npcs.name: Spireling Gholesh
npcs.description: A crass and ambitious man, Gholesh's appearance is a mystery as his face is always hidden behind a leather mask that resembles an ogre. He has secretly thrown in his lot with the League of Miracles and, with their backing, he aspires to take over the Clasp and enjoy all its wealth and prestige.

npcs.name: Spireling Melchior
npcs.description: This clean-faced, curly-haired tiefling with pale blue skin and stubby horns may have a soft, babyish visage, but it belies their powerful physique. They are equally skilled with a sword, axe, or bow, and made their name in underground brawling rings before joining the Clasp.

npcs.name: Spireling Fetch
npcs.description: Creepy and unkempt in appearance, Fetch's gaunt face only distracts from his cunning and skills of keen manipulation.

npcs.name: The Wonderworker
npcs.description: Mysterious enactor of true miracles. All spellwrights hear the authoritative—yet enigmatically distorted—voice of the Wonderworker. The Wonderworker has supposedly appeared in the flesh only three times throughout the league's twenty-four-year history, as a humanoid draped in robes of starlight and wearing a mithral mask. In those moments, they have produced true miracles—raising a castle from the ground in a matter of seconds, halting the rampaging silver dragon Saldarthoryn in her tracks and healing her twisted mind, and stopping the Center Slab of Kraghammer from collapsing into the Pits in a catastrophic mining accident that would have cost countless lives.

npcs.name: Blaine Kraverrogg
npcs.description: Halt-halfling mercenary necromancer. Short and brimming with a malign lust for power, Blaine appears to be a short, skeletally skinny human who hides his lack of stature in billowing black-and-gold robes. He is a member of the Remnants, but pays his bills by doing undercover grave-robbing for the league. He longs to reach the bottom of Shadebarrow, a mysterious crypt somewhere on the Dividing Plains. His obsession with Shadebarrow stems from a hunger for the power of the Demon Prince of Undeath.

npcs.name: Honor Kinnabari
npcs.description: Tiefling blood mage and novice spellwright. As the newest spellwright in the League of Miracles, Honor Kinnabari has a lot to prove. She was granted a chance to prove her quality in the eyes of the Wonderworker when the league was contracted to rebuild the Market Ward of Westruun after it was devastated by a herd of magma landsharks that descended from the Cliffkeep Mountains. Her red eyes and sheet-white skin and horns complement a traditional red-and-white mage’s robe from the reclusive dwarven clans of the Alabaster Sierras. She is fully dedicated to the league, but she is as honorable as her name implies; her fellow spellwrights fear that she could turn traitor, should the unsavory truth of the league be laid plain before her.

npcs.name: High Curator Greisalda Cassios
npcs.description: Half-dragonblood leader of the Cobalt Reserve. The High Curator of the Westruun archive of the Cobalt Soul is a high-cheekboned, bald woman who would appear fully human if not for her slitted, er eyes and the silver scales that run across her head, neck, and upper arms. She is regarded as one of the fastest minds in Tal'Dorei, for she has the rare gift of perfect recall. Monks tremble when her lear, unpretentious voice rings through an archive chamber, for Greisalda remembers acts of justice and personal slights with equal intensity, making her a powerful ally and a furious enemy. She is concerned that corruption is spreading throughout the Tal'Dorei Council.

npcs.name: Greisalda
npcs.description: Regarded as one of the fastest minds in Tal'Dorei, for she has the rare gift of perfect recall. Monks tremble when her clear, unpretentious voice rings through an archive chamber, for Greisalda remembers acts of justice and personal slights with equal intensity, making her a powerful ally and a furious enemy. She is concerned that corruption is spreading throughout the Tal'Dorei Council.

npcs.name: Cressida Holt
npcs.description: The name Cressida Holt is synonymous with style and effortless charisma—and also a blunt, merciless coldness. Cressida is nonbinary, and uses both she and they pronouns interchangeably. Though she's fresh blood to the expositors of the Cobalt Reserve, she has already taken advantage of her license to kill on her espionage missions. They are slim for an ore, but still more muscular than many of their human colleagues. Their assignments take them across Tal'Dorei in search of political corruption. She is currently stationed in Emon to observe a person of interest on the Tal'Dorei Council, where she alternates between lurking on rooftops and striding through ballrooms in fine suits.

npcs.name: Archivist Salomane Rothtree
npcs.description: A haggard, overworked administrator, Archivist Rothtree is known throughout the Cobalt Reserve as someone who tries too hard to prove himself and constantly bites off more than he can chew. Half-ore and half-elf, he has said that he hopes to accomplish as much in his lifetime as an elf could in theirs. He often is tasked with helping adventurers find information. Though he resents the task, he may slowly open up to heroes who treat him well.

npcs.name: Lustran "The Backstabber" Zeth
npcs.description: Human boss of Stilben. Lustran was one of the first Clasp members to turn double agent. By the time anyone realized his betrayal, he had granted the Myriad their foothold in Tal’Dorei in the swampy port city of Stilben. His lean, hungry face and graying hair give him a handsome, intimidating appearance. All Myriad agents in Tal'Dorei respect him, and all members of the Clasp hate him, He revels in his bad reputation as the renowned Backstabber of Stilben.

npcs.name: Tully "The Conclave of One" Dezzeram
npcs.description: Gold dragonblood boss of Emon. Tully's distasteful nickname delights her inner circle in Emon's underground. The Myriad boss of Emon is a position that usually changes hands by the season, thanks to the diligent efforts of the Clasp, but Tully has evaded capture for three years, and grown rich and powerful in her reign of smuggling, trafficking, and grand burglary.

npcs.name: Sylker "The Millionaire" Uttolot
npcs.description: Half-elf boss of Kymal. This gold-eyed half-elf, a former underling of the crime families of Shady Creek Run in Wildemount, joined the Myriad and became the first individual on that continent to hoard one million gold pieces. He has a masterful mind for money, and spearheaded the Myriad’s infiltration of Kymal. "Gold is a disease," he often says, "and I'm bloody sick."

npcs.name: Quinton Puck
npcs.description: Human jeweler, Master of the Unveiled Sight. While he runs a middling jewelry business within Emon, Quinton is secretly the leader of the Unveiled Sight. He is a master of creating and piercing illusions, deciphering ancient script, and all things to do with the magical arts of obscurement and unveiling. He can be recognized by his blood-red spectacles.

npcs.name: Ixrattu Khar
npcs.description: Tiefling vampire, Master of the Devouring Blood. This escapee from the Black Bastille prison in Emon is Tal'Dorei's most infamous mass murderer, who once slaughtered and consumed hundreds of innocents on a deadly killing spree from Kymal to Emon. During her imprisonment, Ixrattu was plagued by shadowy visions of a woman beckoning to her from beyond the bars. The visions pointed her towards weaknesses within the Black Bastille’s guard, and helped her achieve the unthinkable: escape. Once free, she vanished for a year as she scoured the countryside, puzzling over the cryptic whispers of her continuing visions. At the end of her quest was a fateful discovery: within a lightless underground passage, she found the venomous crossbow Condemner, a Vestige of Divergence (see page 204). Now she lurks in Kraghammer, where she trains a network of elite assassins who gleefully dispatch anyone the Unveiled Sight identifies as an enemy of the Remnants.

npcs.name: High Warden Tirelda
npcs.description: Though she is in her twilight years, even by elven standards, High Warden Tirelda is a trusted descendent of Yenlara, founder of Syngorn. She is skilled with magic and blessed with calm wisdom. Thus, she was entrusted with the highest level of responsibility amongst the Wardens—to maintain law, guide society, and preside over all other Wardens.

npcs.name: Verdant Lord Celindar
npcs.description: Head of the Verdant Guard of Syngorn, and an accomplished warrior in their own right, Celindar handles all military strategy and instruction within the forest's bounds. They only return to Syngorn when called by their fellow wardens, and can otherwise constantly be found prowling the Verdant Expanse. They use any pronouns, and have relinquished any sort of gender presentation after receiving a vision from the Arch Heart.

npcs.name: Questra, the Voice of Memory
npcs.description: A renowned historian and a beloved vocalist, Questra is charged with the preservation of Syngorn's history and culture. It's said her most magical songs can control moonlight and bring light even to the Abyss itself. These days, she has grown somewhat unpopular by also singing songs of Syngorn's darker days, for she says true greatness can only be inspired by learning from failure.

npcs.name: Guildrunner Rawndel
npcs.description: One of the oldest living elves within Syngorn, Rawndel is more cunning and insightful than most, allowing him to be a very effective head of commerce, business, and the treasury.

feats.name: Fortune's Grace
feats.description: Your fate-touched essence can cause events to shift in your favor. When you make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can choose to reroll the d20. Alternatively, when a creature attacks you or makes a saving throw against one of your spells or features, you can force that creature to reroll. Once per long rest.
feats.benefits: Reroll a d20 once per long rest

feats.name: Cruel
feats.description: You delight in inflicting pain and anguish upon others. You gain a number of cruelty dice (d6s) equal to your proficiency bonus. You can roll only one cruelty die per turn. When you deal damage to a creature, spend one cruelty die to deal extra damage. When you score a critical hit, spend one cruelty die to gain temporary hit points. When you make a Charisma (Intimidation) check, spend one cruelty die and add the roll.
feats.benefits: Gain cruelty dice (d6s = proficiency bonus) for extra damage, temp hp on crits, or Intimidation bonus

feats.name: Thrown Arms Master
feats.description: You've honed your ability to lob weaponry. Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Simple and martial melee weapons without the thrown property have the thrown property for you. When you miss with a thrown weapon attack using a light weapon, the weapon returns to your grasp at the end of your turn.
feats.benefits: +1 Str or Dex, melee weapons gain thrown property, thrown weapons return on miss

feats.name: Vital Sacrifice
feats.description: You've learned secrets of hemocraft. As a bonus action, you can take 1d6 necrotic damage to gain a blood boon lasting 1 hour. You can expend the boon to gain one of: +1d6 to an attack roll, +2d6 necrotic damage on a hit, or force a creature to subtract the roll from a saving throw.
feats.benefits: Take 1d6 necrotic for a blood boon: bonus to attack, damage, or save penalty

backgrounds.name: Clasp Agent
backgrounds.description: You were a member of the Clasp, a powerful thieves' guild with operations across Tal'Dorei. You know the value of information, the weight of a coin, and the sharp edge of a blade. Whether you left the guild or still work for them, the Clasp's influence follows you.

feature.name: A Favor in Turn
feature.description: You have gained enough clout in the Clasp that you can call in a favor from your contacts whenever you're close enough to a center of syndicate activity. A request for a favor can be no longer than 20 words.

backgrounds.name: Lyceum Student
backgrounds.description: You studied at the Lyceum of Emon, one of Tal'Dorei's most prestigious academies of magic. Your education grants you access to scholarly resources and a network of fellow alumni.

feature.name: Academic Requisition
feature.description: You've gained an ally among the staff, enabling access to certain private areas within the Lyceum and other allied universities. Whenever you're on Lyceum grounds, you can access restricted sections of the library.

backgrounds.name: Reformed Cultist
backgrounds.description: You once belonged to a cult dedicated to one of the Betrayer Gods. Whether you escaped, were cast out, or saw the error of your ways, you now carry the dark knowledge of your former faith.

feature.name: Fell Teachings
feature.description: You were inundated with knowledge about one of the Betrayer Gods. You know by heart everything from their basic commandments to some of their most esoteric secrets.

backgrounds.name: Whitestone Rifle Corps
backgrounds.description: You served in the Whitestone Rifle Corps, an elite military unit armed with the famous firearms of Whitestone. Your training with black powder weapons and dedication to protecting Whitestone sets you apart.

feature.name: Rifle Corps Training
feature.description: You have extensive training with firearms and explosives. You can maintain and repair firearms, and you know where to acquire black powder and ammunition in any major city.

subclasses.name: Path of the Juggernaut
subclasses.description: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Juggernaut become unstoppable forces of destruction, anchoring themselves against any force that would move them and hurling foes through the air.

features.name: Spirit of the Mountain
features.description: While you are raging, you can't be knocked prone or moved along the ground against your will.

features.name: Demolishing Might
features.description: Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 damage to constructs, and deal double damage to objects and structures.

features.name: Resolute Stance
features.description: At the start of your turn, you can assume a defensive stance until the start of your next turn. While in this stance, you can't be grappled, attack rolls against you have disadvantage, and your weapon attacks are made with disadvantage.

features.name: Thunderous Blows
features.description: Starting at 10th level, you can push a creature up to 10 feet when you hit it with a melee attack while you're raging.

features.name: Hurricane Strike
features.description: As a reaction when you push a creature at least 5 feet, you can leap into an unoccupied space next to the creature. The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

subclasses.name: College of Tragedy
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Tragedy know that sorrow and pathos are emotions just as potent as joy and delight. They specialize in the power of tragic storytelling, weaving words and spells together to dramatic and devastating effect.

features.name: Poetry in Misery
features.description: Whenever you or an ally within 30 feet of you rolls a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to regain one expended use of your Bardic Inspiration feature.

features.name: Sorrowful Fate
features.description: When you or an ally forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to change the save type to a Wisdom save instead. If the target fails, roll a Bardic Inspiration die; the target takes psychic damage equal to the result and is plagued with regret for 1 minute.

features.name: Nimbus of Pathos
features.description: You can touch a willing creature as an action and empower it with tragic heroism for 1 minute. The creature gains +4 AC, advantage on attack rolls and saving throws, and deals extra 1d10 radiant damage on hits. Any weapon attack against the creature scores a crit on 18-20. When the effect ends, the creature drops to 0 hit points and is dying. Once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Blood Domain
subclasses.description: The Blood Domain centers around the understanding of the natural life force as it exists within the body, and the divine conduit it can become. Those who take up this domain understand that the power of blood is the power of sacrifice.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons.

features.name: Bloodletting Focus
features.description: When you cast a damage-dealing spell of 1st level or higher with instantaneous duration, any creature with blood that takes damage takes extra necrotic damage equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Crimson Bond
features.description: Form a supernatural bond with a creature you can see. Lasts 1 hour or until concentration breaks. You can learn the target's distance, direction, current hp, and conditions. You can also attempt to see/hear through the target's senses for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Blood Puppet
features.description: Briefly control a Large or smaller creature or corpse with blood within 60 feet. Target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or you control its movement and actions for a short duration.

subclasses.name: Moon Domain
subclasses.description: Clerics of the Moon Domain draw on their divine connection to the moons to wield light and shadow, invoke good fortune and ill favor, and reveal or conceal as they see fit.

features.name: Clarity of Catha
features.description: When a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see makes a Wisdom saving throw, you can use your reaction to grant advantage on the save. Usable proficiency bonus times per long rest.

features.name: Mind of Two Moons
features.description: You can maintain concentration on two Moon Domain spells at once. When you take damage, you make a Constitution save with disadvantage or lose concentration on both.

features.name: Empowered Cantrips
features.description: Your cleric cantrips deal extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

features.name: Eclipse of Ill Omen
features.description: As a bonus action, create dim light in a 60-foot radius. Creatures in the area make saving throws with disadvantage. Once per turn when you deal radiant damage in the area, you can curse a creature: its speed is halved and it can't regain hp. Lasts up to 1 minute (concentration). Once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Blighted
subclasses.description: Druids of the Circle of the Blighted channel corrupted natural energy, binding themselves to poisoned or tainted natural sites and wielding the power of rot and decay.

features.name: Defile Ground
features.description: As a bonus action, corrupt a 10-foot radius patch of land or water within 60 feet for 1 minute. The area is difficult terrain for hostile creatures. Creatures in the area take an extra 1d4 necrotic damage when hit for the first time on a turn. Can move the corruption 30 feet as a bonus action. Once per short or long rest. Radius increases to 20 feet at 10th level, extra damage to 1d6 at 10th and 1d8 at 14th.

features.name: Blighted Shape
features.description: You gain proficiency in Intimidation. While in Wild Shape, your beast form gains +2 AC and darkvision 60 feet (or +60 feet if already has darkvision).

features.name: Call of the Shadowseeds
features.description: When a creature that is not undead or construct takes damage within your Defile Ground, you can use your reaction to summon a blighted sapling that attacks a creature within 5 feet.

features.name: Incarnation of Corruption
features.description: You gain resistance to necrotic damage and +2 AC. When you start your turn within your Defile Ground, you can gain temp hp equal to your proficiency bonus as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Way of the Cobalt Soul
subclasses.description: Monks of the Cobalt Soul dedicate themselves to the pursuit of knowledge, studying their enemies to break through mental and physical defenses.

features.name: Extract Aspects
features.description: As an action, you can touch a creature and learn its damage vulnerabilities, resistances, immunities, and condition immunities.

features.name: Extort Truth
features.description: When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 ki point to force a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the creature can't deliberately lie for up to 10 minutes.

features.name: Mystical Erudition
features.description: You learn one language and gain proficiency in one skill (Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion). Gain additional at 11th and 17th level.

features.name: Mind of Mercury
features.description: Once per turn, if you've already taken your reaction, you may spend 1 ki point to take an additional reaction.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Open Sea
subclasses.description: Paladins who swear the Oath of the Open Sea champion freedom, trusting the guidance of nature and adapting like water to overcome any obstacle.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Marine Layer
features.description: As an action, create a 20-foot radius cloud of fog that moves with you. The area is heavily obscured, but you and creatures within 5 feet treat it as lightly obscured. Lasts 10 minutes.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Fury of the Storm
features.description: As a bonus action, channel the power of storms to grant yourself advantage on attack rolls until the end of your turn.

features.name: Aura of Liberation
features.description: You and allies within 10 feet cannot be grappled or restrained, and ignore underwater movement/attack penalties. Becomes 30 feet at 18th level.

features.name: Stormy Waters
features.description: As a reaction when a creature moves into or out of your reach, it takes 1d12 bludgeoning damage and must make a Strength save or be knocked prone.

features.name: Mythic Swashbuckler
features.description: As an action, gain benefits for 1 minute: advantage on Athletics, climbing speed equal to walking speed, advantage on attacks when within 5 feet of a creature with no other creatures within 5 feet, can Dash/Disengage as a bonus action, advantage on Dexterity checks and saves. Once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Runechild
subclasses.description: Runechild sorcerers manifest their innate magic as runes that appear on their skin, storing magical energy and unleashing it in powerful ways.

features.name: Essence Runes
features.description: You start with 1 essence rune, gaining another each level. When you expend sorcery points, an equal number of essence runes become charged. Charged runes power your Runechild features.

features.name: Glyph of Aegis
features.description: As a bonus action, you or a creature within 30 feet gains protective runes. The next time that creature takes damage within the next hour, it rolls 1d6 per charged rune spent and reduces the damage by the total. Die becomes d8 at 14th level.

features.name: Sigilic Augmentation
features.description: Expend a charged rune as a reaction to gain advantage on Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability checks or saving throws.

features.name: Manifest Inscriptions
features.description: As an action, expend a charged rune to reveal hidden arcane traps, marks, runes, wards, sensors, or glyphs within 60 feet for 1 minute.

features.name: Runic Torrent
features.description: When you cast a spell, expend 2 charged runes to change its damage to force damage. Creatures in the area must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone or pushed 15 feet.

subclasses.name: Blood Magic
subclasses.description: Blood Magic wizards use the magical art of hemocraft, weaving their life force into spells and using blood to fuel their arcane power.

features.name: Blood Channeling
features.description: You can use your own life force to power your magic. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher and have no available spell slots, you can sacrifice hit points equal to 5 times the spell's level to cast it.

features.name: Sanguine Burst
features.description: Whenever you roll damage for a spell you've cast of 1st level or higher, you can take necrotic damage equal to the spell's level to reroll a number of damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one).

features.name: Bond of Mutual Suffering
features.description: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to take damage equal to the damage you took. Cannot be used against constructs or undead. Once per short or long rest (twice at 14th).

features.name: Glyph of Hemorrhaging
features.description: When you damage a creature with a spell, you can curse it for 1 minute. Whenever the cursed creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Thicker Than Water
features.description: Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain additional hp equal to your proficiency bonus. While concentrating, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
